texts.preamble: Vimal Kumar Goyal vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma on 28 November, 2025 The Court Of Ms. Shivali Sharma District Judge-06: Central District, Tis Hazari Court: Delhi Cs Dj No. 11985/16 Digitally signed by In the matter of:- Shivali Shivali Sharma 1. Sh. Vimal Kumar Goyal Sharma Date: S/o Late Sh. Suraj Bhan Goyal 2025.11.28 14:51:21 +0530 2. Smt. Kusum Goyal W/o Sh. Vimal Kumar Goyal Both residents of 1885, Gali Lehaswa, Bazar Sita Ram, Delhi-06. ..........Plaintif versus 1. Sh. Bishan Swaroop Sharma S/o Late Sh. Ram Chander Sharma R/o 1141, Kucha Harjas Mal, Bazar Sita Ram, Delhi-110006.
texts.facts: PLAINTIFF'S CASE: 2. Plaintiffs have filed the present suit alleging themselves to be owners of Shop/Godown no.5 (ad-measuring about 381 sq. ft.), shop/godown no.6 (ad-measuring about 381 sq. ft.), shop/godown no.7 (ad-measuring about 381 sq. ft.) forming part of ground floor along with proportionate right in the land underneath and the common toilet, passages, stair cases and walls and exclusive rights of the roof above the third floor i.e. on flat no.14 and 15, ad-measuring about 891 sq. ft., forming part of property bearing no.VIII/1447, Gali Arya Samaj, Bazar Sita Ram, Delhi-110006 (hereinafter referred to as "suit property") having been purchased by them from defendants no.1 and 2 along with CS DJ No.11985/16 Vimal Kumar Goyal & Anr. Vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma & Ors. Page no.3/18 proportionate rights in the land underneath vide three separate registered Sale Deeds dated 25.11.2003. 3. The defendants no.1 and 3 are carrying on illegal business of supply of water jugs by refrigerating bore-well water from shop/godown no.1 and 2 at ground floor of the suit property in active connivance of all other defendants. No permission has been obtained by the defendants no.1 and 3 from the defendants no.4, 5, 8 and 11 and other concerned authorities for the same. The defendants no.1 and 3 have no right or authority to use underground water resources for commercial sale. The defendants no.1 and 3 are using the electricity directly by committing theft of electricity of the defendant no.7 and have been misusing the same for commercial purposes. Defendants no.1 and 3 have also not obtained any licence from defendants no.6, 8 and 11 for supplying refrigerated drinking water through jugs/bottles. Defendants no.1 and 3 have illegally and unauthorizedly broken the side wall of the shop/godown no.2 and captured the common toilet & passage for storing the water jugs etc. and locked the main gate of the said portion for committing theft of electricity and water from the common toilet so that no one other then the defendants no.1 and 3 can use the common toilet and passage at ground floor of the suit property. Therefore, the plaintiffs are facing great hardship due to aforesaid acts of the defendants no.1 and 3. Previously also, the defendants no.1 and 3 had blocked the common passage and toilet against which the plaintiff no.1 had lodged several complaints with the local authorities and served the defendants no.1, 10 and 11 with the legal notice dated 08.06.2012. Page no.4/18 Thereafter, the defendants no.1 and 3 had removed the blockage and plaintiffs were able to use the facility of the common passage and toilet. 4. The defendants no.1 and 3 have started parking 7-8 cycle rickshaws without any licence and being used for supplying water jugs/bottles to different customers in the gali infront of the suit property thereby illegally and unauthorizedly blocking the egress and ingress of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs had lodged complaints with the defendants no.8 to 11 against the defendants no.1 and 3 on different dates but all in vain. Therefore, the plaintiffs as well as their tenants are suffering a lot as their day to day business is being hampered and the acts of defendants no. 1 and 3 are also causing nuisance and health hazard to the plaintiffs and also monetary losses. The plaintiffs have also served legal Vimal Kumar Goyal vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29460548/ 3 notice dated 16.09.2015 through their Counsel on all the defendants. No reply of the said legal notice has been received till date. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the present suit for permanent and mandatory injunction against the defendants seeking the following reliefs : I. A decree of mandatory injunction thereby directing the defendants no.1 and 3 to immediately restore the wall of the shop/godown no.2 of the suit property and to remove the water jugs/bottles which are being illegally and unauthorizedly stored by the defendants no.1 and 3 in the common toilet and passage at the ground floor of the suit property. II. A decree of mandatory injunction thereby directing the defendants no. 4 to 11 to take necessary, proper and immediate action against the illegal and unauthorized acts of the defendants CS DJ No.11985/16 Vimal Kumar Goyal & Anr. Vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma & Ors. Page no.5/18 no.1 and 3 and to check the health hazard or misuse of the underground water resources and theft of electric power. III. A decree of permanent injunction thereby restraining the defendants no.1 and 3 from parking any cycle rickshaw in the gali in front of the suit property. IV. A decree for a sum of Rs.3,29,000/- towards damages and losses suffered by the plaintiffs and their tenants till the date of filing of the suit and a sum of Rs.1000/- per day from the date of filing of the suit till restoration of the wall of the shop/godown no.2 of the suit property towards passage and removal of the nuisance and encroachment from the ground floor of the suit property. DEFENDANT'S CASE: 5. Defendant no.1 and 3 filed their joint Written Statement preliminarily objecting to the suit of the plaintiffs on the ground that the plaintiffs are not the owners of the suit property and even denied the ownership rights of the plaintiffs in respect to the land underneath and common toilet, passage, stair cases and walls. It is stated that three Sale Deeds all dated 25.11.2003 in respect of the three godowns of the suit property were executed, however, sale consideration mentioned in the said Sale Deeds were never paid by the plaintiffs. In fac, the cheques mentioned in the Sale Deeds were never presented for encashment at the request of the plaintiffs because the plaintiffs promised to issue fresh cheques. However, later on the plaintiffs back tracked and did not pay sale consideration to the owners of these three godown i.e. CS DJ No.11985/16 Vimal Kumar Goyal & Anr. Vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma & Ors. Page no.6/18 defendants no.1 and 2. Due to non-payment of sale consideration, the possession of godown no.5 was never given to the plaintiffs by its owners. The plaintiffs had got sale deeds executed by playing fraud upon the defendants no.1 and 2 and therefore, all these Sale Deeds are null and void. The right, title or interest in respect of the suit property is deemed to have not been created and/or conferred upon the plaintiffs. The defendants have denied all the allegations made by the plaintiffs in the plaint and have pleaded that plaintiffs are not entitled to the reliefs prayed. A separate Written Statement was filed by defendant no.4 wherein suit was preliminarily objected to on the grounds that registration of bore-wells has to be done and permission for extraction of ground water is required to be obtained from the competent authority i.e. Delhi Jal Board. The area in Gali Arya Samaj, Bazar Sita Ram, Delhi, near Chandni Chowk falls in New Delhi district and the same is under regulation of ground water development and management of NCT of Delhi in terms of Lt. Governor, NCT Delhi notification no.F8(348)/EA/Env/09/2246 dated 12.07.2010 issued by Department of Environment and Forests and Wildlife, NCT Delhi. 7. Defendant no.6 also filed its separate Written Statement and stated that the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Foor Additives) Regulations, 2011 prescribed standards for "Packaged Drinking Water" but bore well water supplied in jugs does not come under the purview of the Food Safety Regulations. Defendants no.7 and 8 have also filed their separate Written Statements preliminarily objecting that the present suit on the ground that the same is not maintainable and is liable to be rejected under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC as there is no cause of action against the answering defendants. REPLICATION: 9. Replications were filed to the Written Statements of the defendant no.1, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 wherein the contents of the Written Statements were denied except the admissions made and the contents of the plaint were reiterated. RELEVANT MISCELLANEOUS ORDERS 10. Vide order dated 06.12.2016 it was observed that no Written Statement had been filed on behalf of defendants no.9 to 11 who were Government functionary and there was no case to dispute or admit the averments made in the plaint by them. Accordingly, they were exempted from filing the written statement. 11. Vide order dated 11.07.2017 right of defendant no.6 to file Written Statement was closed. 12. On an admission made by the plaintiffs in an application under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC read with Order 1 Rule 10 CPC to the effect that the defendants had stopped the business of supply of water jugs, defendants no.4 to 8 were deleted from the array of parties vide order dated 06.11.2019. At the stage of final arguments, on 15.11.2025 plaintiff no.1 had given a statement on behalf of both the plaintiffs to the effect that they had sought several reliefs of mandatory and permanent injunction as well as compensation. However, most of the reliefs had become infructuous and the only reliefs which they were pressing were (i) a decree of mandatory injunction in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants no.1 and 3 thereby directing them to immediately restore the wall of the shop/godown no.2 in the site plan Ex.PW1/5 at point X and Y and (ii) a money decree for a sum of Rs.3,29,000/- in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants no.1 and 3 towards damages and losses suffered by the plaintiff and their tenants till the date of the filing of the suit and further a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day from the date of filing of the suit till the restoration of the wall of the shop/godown no. 2 shown at point X and Y in the site plan Ex. PW-1/5. ISSUES: 15. After completion of pleadings, the following issues were framed vide order dated 13.02.2018 : I. Sh. Dipanshu is a summoned witness from the Office of SDM Kotwali, Daryaganj. He produced the summoned record i.e. Copy of complaint dated 11.08.2014 received in the office of EE (Planning), Water-1 DJB on 26.08.2014 regarding extraction of ground water/illegal boring (Mark A) and complaint received on 18.05.2015 from Vimal Kumar Goyal which is Ex. PW-2/1. He deposed that the department had taken action on the complaint and issued notice dated 24.09.2014 to the owner/occupier of the concerned property. Copy of the notice is Ex. PW-2/2. CS DJ No.11985/16 . PW-3 HC Satyaveer is a summoned witness from the Office ACP Kamla Market. He produced the summoned record in respect of the complaint dated 13.04.2015 made by Sh. Vimal Kumar Goyal Vimal Kumar Goyal vs Bishan Swaroop Sharma on 28 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29460548/ 6 which was registered against Entry No. 118 dated 13.04.2015 and forwarded to SHO Hauz Quazi on 13.04.2015 for necessary action. The copy of the register is Ex. PW-3/1. 20. PW-4 Constable Pawan Kumar is a summoned witness from PS Hauz Quazi. He produced the summoned record i.e. a complaint dated 12.01.2015 made by Vimal Kumar Goyal (Ex. PW-4/1) and the copy of the complaint register along with action taken report which is Ex. PW-4/2. He also produced copy of order dated 22.07.2019 (Mark B) as per which complaint register upto 31.12.2012 had been destroyed. He also produced copy of complaint dated 09.05.2011 which was received in their office by HC Manju Bala on 09.05.2011 and the copy of which is Mark C. 21. Plaintiff no.1 Sh.Vimal Kumar Goyal examined himself as PW-5 and stated and reiterated on oath the contents of the plaint in his examination-in- chief recorded before the Court vide his affidavit Ex.PW-5/A. He relied upon the following documents:- (i) Ex.PW1/1 (OSR) is the copy of registered Sale Deed dated 25.11.2003 executed by Sh. Puran Chand and Sh. Bishan Swaroop in favour of Smt. Kusum Goyal. (ii) Ex.PW1/2 (OSR) is the copy of registered Sale Deed dated 25.11.2003 executed by Sh. Puran Chand and Sh. Bishan Swaroop in favour of Smt. Kusum Goyal. . Page no.11/18 (iii) Ex.PW1/3 (OSR) is the copy of registered Sale Deed dated 25.11.2003 executed by Sh. Puran Chand and Sh. Bishan Swaroop in favour of Sh. Vimal Kumar Goyal. (iv) Ex.PW5/4 (OSR) (colly) is the copy of legal notice dt. 08.06.2012 along with postal receipts. (v) Ex.PW5/5 is the site plan of entire ground floor of the suit property. (vi) Ex. PW-4/1 is the copy of complaint dt. 12.01.2015 made to SHO PS Hauz Quazi. (vii) Mark D (colly) are the copies of complaints given to various departments. (viii) Ex.PW5/7 is the Legal Notice. (ix) Ex. PW-5/8 (colly) are the 22 postal receipts in respect of Legal Notice. 22. PW-1 to PW-4 were not subjected to cross examination however, PW-5 was cross examined at length on behalf of defendants no. 1 and 3 but not on behalf of other defendants. 23. No other witness was examined on behalf of the plaintiffs and their PE was closed vide order dated 15.09.2025.
